definitions.explanation: The main upright part of a plant that supports the leaves, flowers, and fruit. Used for all types of plants, from flowers to vegetables.

examples.japanese: ブロッコリーは{茎|くき}も{食|た}べられる。
examples.english: You can eat broccoli stems too.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}で{茎|くき}が{折|お}れて、{花|はな}が{全部|ぜんぶ}だめになった。
examples.english: The stems broke in the typhoon, and all the flowers were ruined.

notes:
{茎|くき} refers to the stem or stalk of any plant — the part that supports leaves, flowers, and fruit.

USAGE:
Applies to flowers, vegetables, and herbs alike. For tree trunks, use {幹|みき} instead. For mushroom stems, {軸|じく} is more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {茎|くき}を{切|き}る: to cut a stem
- {茎|くき}が{伸|の}びる: a stem grows/extends
- {茎|くき}が{折|お}れる: a stem breaks
- {太|ふと}い{茎|くき}: thick stalk
- {茎|くき}わかめ: stem wakame (a popular snack)

IN COOKING:
Many vegetable stems are edible and commonly used in Japanese cooking. ブロッコリーの{茎|くき} (broccoli stems) and セロリの{茎|くき} (celery stalks) are everyday ingredients.

RELATED WORDS:
- {幹|みき}: tree trunk
- {枝|えだ}: branch
- {根|ね}: root
- {葉|は}: leaf
